prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant produces compliant potable water; boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded. Ironwood: automatic/withdrawal-limited; starts require proven hydraulic/motor/isolation/interlock readiness; faults/local-control/trips inhibit/alarm/stop. Chief Operator authorizes justified manual operation/Storm Intake Mode; restore automation; recovery requires approved stability. Raw Water Screen Channel sends Rake Torque Snapshot; high-high requires field confirmation. Maintenance Planner (Quarry) uses snapshot before rake-work release. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies identity. Chief Operator confirms dose; Duty Engineer approves rapid-turbidity changes. Feedback loss requires verified-safe/fixed dosing/grabs; coagulation failure requires feed/mixing/Chlorine Contact Basin assessment. Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment/priority grabs. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) records turbidity/headloss; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note. Return requires rinse-to-waste/stability. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage/production; changes require header-plan coordination. Backwash Recovery Tank returns require consequential sampling. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples/sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set; Laboratory Technician sends Sample Chain Slip. Preserve custody/mismatches; invalid samples troubleshooting-only; release requires quality-control review/correction/rejection. Field readings provisional; Duty Engineer reviews differences; notify Chief Operator of contradictory confirmation. Storm instability increases sampling. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains synchronized process/results timestamps. Work orders require approved windows, responsible persons, return conditions, equipment/isolations/parts/closure evidence; Chief Operator reviews next-day capacity/quality/demand; Duty Engineer may defer. Identify electrical/hydraulic/pneumatic/chemical/stored-energy hazards; craft verifies isolation locally, operations acknowledges before intervention; Ironwood additionally requires tags/turnover acknowledgment. Preserve filtration capacity. Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; approved routes/areas/operator-observed times only. Inspect dosing-transfer hoses/containment/washdown; basin work requires ventilation/gas monitoring/communications. Shift turnover includes isolations/limits/unavailability/abnormalities. Distribution Dispatcher receives advance header/North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station maintenance-impact notice. Residuals Hauler removes residuals/backwash.

New part:
S118: When Storm Intake Mode is active, discretionary work is reviewed again because debris loading, chemical demand, and operator workload may change quickly.
S119: A Chlorine Residual Alarm during maintenance causes the affected task to pause until operations confirms whether the alarm is process-related or maintenance-induced.
S120: The Laboratory Technician supports work control by confirming sampling needs and by reporting any acceptance concern that could delay equipment return.
S121: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench remains available for maintenance-related samples when water quality confirmation is required before a unit is returned to service.
S122: Evidence for return to service may include local inspection results, functional test readings, instrument response checks, sample results, and operator acceptance comments.
S123: Equipment is returned to service only after temporary jumpers, bypasses, tools, spare parts, and barriers have been removed or formally accepted for continued use.
S124: If a post-maintenance test fails, the work order stays open and the Chief Operator determines whether the equipment remains isolated or can be operated under restriction.
S125: The SCADA Historian Server retains operating data needed to compare pre-work and post-work performance for pumps, dosing systems, filters, and level controls.
S126: Following maintenance closeout, disinfection control is returned to normal service only after the Chief Operator confirms that the chlorine feed controls, residual instruments, and level indications are responding consistently in the SCADA Historian Server.
S127: The Chlorine Contact Basin is operated to maintain the required contact time under the current production rate, basin level, and measured disinfectant residual.
S128: Operators adjust chlorine feed gradually so that changes in residual do not outrun mixing and contact time through the Chlorine Contact Basin.
S129: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm occurs, the control room verifies analyzer sample flow, compares the reading with a grab sample result, and holds any planned production increase until the condition is understood.
S130: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmatory residual results when analyzer drift, sample line fouling, or an unexpected residual trend is suspected.
S131: The Clearwell Level Controller maintains normal storage within established operating limits that protect disinfectant contact, reserve volume, and high-service pump suction conditions.
S132: Low clearwell level interlocks are configured to prevent pump operation from drawing the storage volume below the minimum level needed for safe hydraulic operation.
S133: High clearwell level alarms give operators time to reduce production or adjust downstream pumping before overflow conditions develop.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
